halfLives.notes: Health Canada (2018) citing Vikesland et al. (2001): half-life of over 300 h at 4 °C, pH 7.5. V1 uses 300 h as a conservative implemented bound (slightly faster decay than 'over 300 h').
Health Canada (2018) citing Vikesland et al. (2001): half-life decreases to 75 h at 35 °C, pH 7.5.

freeAmmonia.notes: V1 does not apply an unverified free-ammonia rate modifier or autodecomposition yield. Ammonia is mixed and advected only.

notImplemented.roy2020SimplifiedChemicalModel: Equations from Roy, Sathasivan, Kastl (2020) DOI 10.1016/j.scitotenv.2020.140410 were not retrieved in implementable form.
notImplemented.wntrBatchChloramineDecay: WNTR library batch_chloramine_decay is a multi-species batch/pipe example with empty tank_reactions and no temperature dependence. Not a drop-in WDS model.
notImplemented.fullVikeslandJafvertValentineMsx: Unified chloramine autodecomposition (HOCl/NH3/NH2Cl/NHCl2/carbonate) is not the V1 residual operator.

validityRange.notes: Half-lives are reported at pH 7.5. Temperature outside 4–35 °C is an extrapolation of the two-point van 't Hoff fit. pH, Cl/N and alkalinity are validated configuration, not invented kinetic terms.

references.citation: Vikesland, Ozekin, Valentine (2001). Monochloramine Decay in Model and Distribution System Waters. Water Research 35(7), 1766–1776.
Health Canada (2018). Chloramines in Drinking Water — Guideline Technical Document for Public Consultation. Reports Vikesland pH 7.5 half-lives: >300 h at 4 °C and 75 h at 35 °C.

Roy, Sathasivan, Kastl (2020). Simplified chemical chloramine decay model for water distribution systems. Science of the Total Environment 741, 140410. Inspected as a primary source; coefficients were not implemented because implementable equations were not confirmed.
